source.title: Training Compute-Optimal Protein Language Models
source.authors: Xingyi Cheng; Bo Chen; Pan Li; Jing Gong; Jie Tang; Le Song

record.tranche_reason: The study fits scaling relations in protein language models and reports conditions that qualify them, including objective-specific exponents and overfitting when a limited dataset is repeated.
record.gate_note: Results reported from the study's own protein-model experiments are included. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not rows. The paper also reports many generation metrics; they are not included as scaling-law results because they do not measure how downstream performance varies predictably with scale.
record.test_reason: The study fits its own loss and compute-optimal power laws on about 260 protein language models, from 1e18 to 1e21 FLOPs. It also tests repeated data, transfer, fitting-method variants and MoE models. Protein sequences are a new modality, so this is T3 rather than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that CLM-to-MLM transfer follows a scaling law: about 20% of compute on CLM pre-training saves compute (7.7× vs 10×). They say their compute-optimal 7.2B CLM and 10.7B MLM beat PROGEN2-xlarge and ESM-2 3B at similar compute. They describe these as validations of the laws, not tests of loss prediction.
record.recipe_differences: Protein-sequence models rather than natural-language models; uses CLM and MLM, UniMeta200B, and IsoFLOPs profiling with study-specific fits.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported exponents and outcomes differ between CLM and MLM. Repeating UR50/S causes diminishing returns or overfitting, while the expanded UniMeta200B dataset is reported to avoid those effects. An alternative combined-loss fit is reported to give trends close to the IsoFLOPs fit.

fits_no_version.finding: At equal compute (1.68e22), the re-allocated 10.7B MLM beats ESM-2 3B on 7 of 8 tasks; contact prediction ties and localization is lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal re-allocation improves downstream performance at a fixed budget.

fits_no_version.finding: The 7.2B CLM (1.14e22 FLOPs) beats PROGEN2-xlarge (1.34e22) on OOD perplexity, pLDDT (78.69 vs 74.33) and cluster diversity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal re-allocation improves generation quality at similar compute.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The loss-law exponents are reported without uncertainty estimates. The study says fitting may be affected when data exceeds 200 billion tokens or when dataset quality or quantity changes. The compute-optimal fits use a finite set of FLOP budgets, and the downstream comparison is not a test of out-of-sample loss prediction.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only details for the repeated-data curves and additional generation comparisons in Section 5.1 were not extracted as scaling-law or downstream-predictability rows; the text gives some generation summary metrics, but those compare models on generation measures rather than a fitted downstream performance-versus-scale relation.

untested.parts: Natural-language text models; only protein sequences are tested.
The 7.2B and 10.7B models were sized by extrapolating fits to about 1.7e22 FLOPs, but predicted versus realised loss is never reported.
Depth and width at fixed parameter count are not isolated.
Image, video and other non-protein modalities.
No fitted downstream-versus-scale or downstream-versus-loss relation.
Parameter-counting conventions and training schedules are not varied.

missing.what: Transfer scaling coefficients: MLM from CLM Bt = 11.133, αt = −0.038; CLM from MLM 7.191, −0.024.
MoE allocation exponents close to dense: CLM 0.57 vs 0.58, MLM 0.74 vs 0.77.
IsoLoss fit gives model-size exponents 0.77 (MLM) and 0.57 (CLM).
Combined-fit coefficients: CLM α 0.367, β 0.496; MLM α 0.042, β 0.099.
At equal loss 1.98, 880M MLM outperforms 7.2B CLM on contact prediction.
ESM-2 650M, 3B and 15B give closely matching contact prediction results.
At equal FLOPs, 2.8B on 1T tokens (about 5 epochs) vs 10.7B on 265B gives similar OOD PPL (10.33 vs 10.21).

record.verdict_notes: Treated protein LMs as a new setting for V1/V3 and as a modality test for V5. The fits use only 7 budgets (1e18–1e21) and report no uncertainty. The authors caution that fits may change beyond 200B tokens or with different data. The reader's V6 links were misplaced: the 10.7B vs ESM-2 rows compare models at equal compute, not at different scales.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-language models and other model families.
No held-out test of loss predictions from small runs against runs orders of magnitude larger is reported.
No direct comparison to both original studies' allocation prescriptions on the same setup.
The study does not isolate depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Image, video, and other modalities; fine-tuning and transfer do not receive a separate power-law loss test.
No fitted relationship or test of downstream-task predictability across a scale sweep.
The study does not systematically vary parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, or fitting methods to estimate their effects on exponents.
